Overview

How to use this guide

One set of rules, three ways in. The guide teaches the thinking. The kit builds it into the tools you already use, so a chart starts on-brand and gets checked before it goes out.

Clear charts move decisions forward. When the point is obvious, a meeting spends its time on what to do, not on what the chart means. Top consulting firms hold every chart to that standard; the kit makes it the easy path, and every rule can be checked by you, a reviewer or an AI assistant.

Inspired by the structure of a leading consulting firm's public guide, rebuilt for McKesson's brand. Workforce Innovation uses it first, so the examples are workforce data; the rules are the same for any team.

In PowerPoint and Excel

Start from the template

Read Fundamentals once, then use the chart pages as you build. Keep the cheat sheet next to you.

  • PowerPoint template and starter deck
  • Excel chart workbook with the palette
  • One-page cheat sheet and chart chooser
  • Power BI report theme

In code

Python, R, Power BI, the web

Each chart page links to tested code. Themes are generated from one token file, so every tool matches.

  • mckviz for matplotlib and Plotly
  • CSS variables, Plotly and Vega-Lite themes
  • theme_mck() for ggplot2
  • mv.lint(fig) to check a chart

With an AI assistant

Copilot, Claude, coding agents

The same playbook, read by the assistant: in this repo through AGENTS.md, anywhere else as a skill or one rules file. It checks its own work.

  • AGENTS.md: workflow and rules
  • mck-chart skill: question to QA
  • dist/agents/mck-viz-rules.md
  • Cookbook pages with runnable snippets

The five steps behind every chart

1 Question. Write the question the chart answers in one sentence.

2 Chart. Pick the chart from the question type, not from habit.

3 Build. Grey first, then color only what the headline names.

4 Headline. Compute the finding, then write it as a sentence.

5 QA. Run the checklist and look at the rendered chart.
